_about: Every Slither finding on contracts/src, reviewed. CI (slither-gate.py) fails on any finding not listed here. Keys are the detector plus the finding's first line with source locations removed.

findings.key: arbitrary-send-eth: PasskeyAccount.execute(address,uint256,bytes,uint64,WebAuthn.WebAuthnAuth) sends eth to arbitrary user
findings.reason: Intended: execute is the account owner's generic call. It runs only after a WebAuthn signature by the account's passkey over (chainId, account, nonce, target, value, dataHash, deadline), verified on-chain; the nonce prevents replay.
Same call as above; a generic account must use a low-level call. The success flag is checked and the revert data is bubbled up.
The target is chosen and signed by the passkey owner; a call to address(0) only wastes the owner's own transaction and moves nothing it did not sign.

findings.key: uninitialized-local: VerdictVault._createPot(address,bytes32,address,address[],uint16[],address,uint64).sum is a local variable never initialized
findings.reason: False positive: a uint256 accumulator that starts at its default 0 by design (sum of shares, checked == 10,000).

findings.key: uninitialized-local: MultisigResolver.isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes).last is a local variable never initialized
findings.reason: False positive: starts at address(0) on purpose so the first recovered signer passes the strictly-increasing check.
The clone address is computed beforehand with predictDeterministicAddress and is the same value; the call reverts if deployment fails.

findings.key: unused-return: MultisigResolver.isValidSignature(bytes32,bytes) ignores return value by (signer,err,None) = ECDSA.tryRecover(digest,sig)
findings.reason: Only the third value (the raw signature-s error detail) is ignored; signer and err are both checked.
The external call is to the trusted, immutable VerdictVault (claim of the book's own balance), the function is nonReentrant, and the claim bit and claimed total are written before any call.
External calls are to the immutable vault and USDC (trySafeTransfer); payout is nonReentrant and the cursor/settled state is the only control flow state.
swept is set before any external call; nonReentrant; calls go to the immutable vault and USDC only.
The call is to the freshly deployed clone's initialize; the event order has no security effect.

findings.key: costly-loop: GuaranteeBook._send(uint256,address,uint256,bool) has costly operations inside a loop:
findings.reason: totalClaimable is updated only when a transfer fails (blocklisted customer), at most 50 customers per guarantee and paid in batches.
Lock times and deadlines are minutes to days apart; validator timestamp drift (seconds) cannot change an outcome.

findings.key: timestamp: GuaranteeBook.enrol(uint256,address) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.reason: Enrolment lock time; seconds of drift are irrelevant at this granularity.
Root lock and claim deadlines; coarse windows.
Root lock time; coarse window.
Claim deadline 30 days after resolution; coarse window.

findings.key: timestamp: MerkleBook.sweep(uint256) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.reason: Sweep after the claim deadline; coarse window.
Rejects deadlines in the past.

findings.key: timestamp: VerdictVault.fund(uint256,uint256) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.reason: No funding after the deadline; coarse window.
Same as fund.

findings.key: timestamp: VerdictVault.resolve(uint256,bool,bytes) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.reason: Resolution allowed until deadline + grace (1 h); seconds of drift do not matter.

findings.key: timestamp: VerdictVault.expire(uint256) uses timestamp for comparisons
findings.reason: Expiry after deadline + grace; the complement of resolve.
Signature deadline (minutes); drift cannot extend it meaningfully.
